answer_findings.RLSECURITY-1: security lens, medium: ANSI escape sequences from an attacker-controlled GitHub comment survive partial stripping and are emitted to the user's terminal via printf. (core/claim/claim.sh: "holder_value="$(sed -e 's/^"holder":[[:space:]]*"\(.*\)"$/\1/' \             -e 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[mK]//g' <<< "$raw_holder" || true)""; happens when: An attacker who can post or edit a comment on the GitHub issue embeds ANSI escape bytes (cursor movement, screen-clear, OSC title sequences, etc.) in the <!-- zbuild-holder: --> field. The sed pattern only strips CSI sequences ending in m or K; other ESC-prefixed sequences survive into _ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER and are then sent to stderr via printf '%s\n' "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER:-unknown}" >&2, where any terminal emulator will interpret them.; fix: code; ACCEPTED IF: The holder string extracted from outside input is stripped of all ANSI/terminal escape sequences before being printed to stderr, using a strip that is at least as broad as the event bus's _eb_strip_ansi (which covers CSI sequences ending in any letter or ~ and bare ESC-X pairs).)
answer_findings.RLSECURITY-2: security lens, low: The holder is JSON-encoded by escaping only double-quote characters, leaving literal backslashes unescaped and producing structurally invalid JSON. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: "escaped_holder="$(printf '%s' "$holder" | sed 's/"/\\"/g' || true)""; happens when: A holder string that contains a backslash (e.g. a Windows path or any attacker-modified holder) generates output such as {"acquired": false, "holder": "foo\bar"}, which is invalid JSON (bare backslash). Downstream extraction in claim.sh uses grep/sed rather than jq, so there is no current injection path, but any future JSON consumer of the coordinator's stdout would mis-parse the response.; fix: code; ACCEPTED IF: The holder embedded in the JSON stdout of claim_coordinator_claim is fully JSON-string-safe: at minimum backslash is escaped to \\ before double-quote is escaped, so the value could be re-parsed by a standards-conforming JSON tool.)
answer_findings.RLREDTEAM-1:
red-team lens, medium: The sed pattern that sanitizes the holder string strips only CSI SGR (m) and EL (K) sequences, leaving cursor-movement, clear-screen, cursor-position, and OSC sequences intact, so those bytes reach the operator's terminal via printf '%s
' and are executed as terminal control sequences. (core/claim/claim.sh: "holder_value="$(sed -e 's/^"holder":[[:space:]]*"\(.*\)"$/\1/' \             -e 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[mK]//g' <<< "$raw_holder" || true)""; happens when: An attacker who can post a crafted holder comment includes a sequence such as '\x1b[2J' (clear screen) or '\x1b]0;evil\x07' (window-title injection) in the holder string. The sed pattern does not match these sequences because their terminators are not 'm' or 'K', so they survive into _ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER and are written verbatim to the operator's terminal when the refused run calls printf '%s
' "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER:-unknown}" >&2.; fix: code; ACCEPTED IF: The holder string passed to printf '%s
' on refusal contains no terminal control sequences — meaning the sanitization applied to the extracted holder before it is stored in _ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER strips all CSI sequences (any letter terminator) and all bare-ESC-prefixed sequences, at minimum matching the coverage of the event-bus's _eb_strip_ansi pattern.)
answer_findings.RLCORRECTNESS-1: correctness lens, medium: The JSON holder extraction in `zbuild_claim_acquire` uses `grep -o '"holder":[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"'`; the `[^"]*` class stops at the first `"` character, so a holder whose JSON-escaped form contains `\"` (an escaped double-quote, written by `claim_coordinator_claim`'s `sed 's/"/\\"/g'`) is silently truncated — the regex matches only the bytes before the escaped quote. (core/claim/claim.sh: "raw_holder="$(grep -o '"holder":[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"' <<< "$json_out" || true)""; happens when: A holder string containing a literal double-quote character (e.g. a machine name or run-id containing `"`); `claim_coordinator_claim` JSON-escapes it to `\"`, but `[^"]*` stops at the unescaped `"` byte, returning a truncated `raw_holder` to the outer `sed` extraction, which then strips only up to the first `"` it sees.; fix: code; ACCEPTED IF: The holder string as printed in the run's refusal output is identical to the holder string embedded in the run-status comment's `<!-- zbuild-holder: -->` field, even when that string contains a double-quote character.)
answer_findings.RLSRE-1: sre lens, medium: claim_coordinator_release always returns 0 regardless of whether _ccgl_remove_label succeeds, so the advisory warning path in zbuild_claim_release is unreachable and label-removal failures are completely silent. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: "_ccgl_remove_label "$issue" "zbuild:claimed"     return 0"; happens when: On any run exit, zbuild_claim_release calls plugin_hook_call, which calls claim_coordinator_release. For the gh backend, if `gh issue edit --remove-label` fails (network error, rate limit, permission denied), _ccgl_remove_label returns non-zero and all gh stderr is already suppressed (`>/dev/null 2>&1`). claim_coordinator_release ignores the return code and exits 0. zbuild_claim_release's `plugin_hook_call ... || { printf 'release hook failed...' }` handler never fires. The label silently remains, and every subsequent run on that issue is refused with 'already claimed' and no log explaining why the previous release failed.; fix: code; ACCEPTED IF: claim_coordinator_release propagates _ccgl_remove_label's non-zero exit so the advisory warning in zbuild_claim_release fires when the gh backend fails to remove the label; or the design is amended to explicitly accept that label-removal failures are entirely silent with no log or event.)
